bihar_raw_news.title: India From digital to AI public infrastructure | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: October 06, 2026 India: From digital to AI public infrastructure Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Rajesh Seth India may be preparing for its next big digital leap. And this time, it could be about putting intelligence on top of the digital infrastructure that already exists. On September 21, Rajiv Kumar, President and Managing Director of Microsoft India, said India is on a roadmap to move from Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) to AI public infrastructure over the next five years. He specifically referred to Aadhaar, UPI and Digi Yatra as examples of the country’s successful DPI. The statement raises a simple question: what exactly is AI public infrastructure? To understand this, think of India’s DPI as a network of digital highways. Aadhaar provides a digital identity. UPI provides a common rail for digital payments. Digi Locker provides a way to access digital documents. These are not individual services competing with private companies. They are common infrastructure on which thousands of public and private services can be built. Adding an intelligent layer AI public infrastructure could add an intelligent layer to these digital highways. Instead of simply enabling a transaction, an AI-enabled system could understand a person’s language, analyse information, personalise a service or help the person navigate a complicated process. In simple terms, DPI connects people digitally; AI infrastructure could help technology understand and assist them. This idea is not entirely theoretical. At the India AI Impact Summit in February, Nandan Nilekani, one of the architects of India’s digital public infrastructure, argued that the important question is how quickly AI can be productively diffused among people. Drawing a parallel with UPI, he said open networks allow many innovators to build applications using AI. He also argued that AI agents could remove complexity for users by allowing them to interact in their own language. That is an important distinction. India does not necessarily need to build every AI application itself. Just as UPI created an open architecture on which banks and technology companies could build payment services, an AI-enabled public infrastructure could allow many organisations to build applications for healthcare, agriculture, education and public services. The Singapore model Singapore provides an interesting glimpse of how such an approach can work. Its Government Technology Agency says it is building shared AI tools and data infrastructure for Government agencies. These include AI-powered citizen-service chatbots, productivity tools for public officers and analytics platforms. Instead of every agency developing its own AI system from scratch, shared infrastructure can reduce duplication and speed up deployment. Singapore’s updated National AI Strategy, released in May this year, also calls for AI to be embedded more deeply across Government to improve public services. But there is an important lesson here for India: AI infrastructure is not simply about computers and data centres. The World Bank’s latest research, based on Government responses from 60 economies, shows that AI adoption in Governments is already widespread but often shallow. national_raw_news.content: India and Switzerland today inked five agreements following bilateral talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Swiss President Guy Parmelin in New Delhi. These agreements are on Migration and Mobility Partnership, Exchange of Young Professionals, Promotion and Collaboration on Transportation Technologies, Mobility Systems and Infrastructure in Identified Areas, Letter of Intent between Department of Science and Technology and Swiss National Science Foundation and Implementation Arrangement for cooperation in Innovation, Technology Transfer and Entrepreneurship. In a joint press meet, Prime Minister Modi appreciated Swiss President Guy Parmelin’s commitment to India-Switzerland relations. He said that India implemented the historic Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement with the European Free Trade Association, EFTA, countries last October. Mr Modi noted that the agreement was India’s first Free Trade Agreement with a European economic bloc. He described it as an ambitious framework for investment, innovation, employment and shared prosperity. The Prime Minister highlighted that under the agreement, India aims to attract 100 billion US dollars in investment and create ten lakh direct jobs over the next 15 years. Prime Minister Modi said that India and Switzerland have taken several important decisions to enhance market access for Indian exports in Switzerland and further facilitate investment between the two countries. He said, this will increase exports of Indian agricultural products, pharmaceuticals, textiles and engineering goods to Switzerland. Mr Modi said that at the same time, India will attract new Swiss investments in important sectors, such as biotechnology, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing and sustainability. Prime Minister said, through these initiatives, the two nations will work together to develop trusted supply chains and reliable solutions for the entire world. He said, both the nations today identified new possibilities for cooperation in military exchanges and defence production. Mr Modi said the they have also agreed to further deepen cooperation in nuclear energy. The Prime Minister said, the friendship between India and Switzerland goes back centuries. He said, in the 19th century, Swami Vivekananda saw a glimpse of the Himalayas in the Swiss Alps. Mahatma Gandhi also spent time in Switzerland and interacted with its people. Mr Modi said, the memories of these historic visits continue to resonate in the friendship even today. President Parmelin arrived in New Delhi this morning on a three-day state visit to India, accompanied by a high-level delegation comprising senior officials and business leaders. He was received by Minister of State for Road Transport and Highways Ajay Tamta at the airport. The visiting dignitary was accorded a ceremonial welcome at the forecourt of Rashtrapati Bhavan. President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the Swiss President. He was given a tri-services guard of honour. Talking to reporters after the ceremonial welcome, Mr Parmelin said that the visit is an excellent opportunity to emphasise the importance that both Switzerland and India attach to this relationship. He said, the relationship between the two countries is built on shared democratic values, as well as on trust and mutual respect. Swiss President said that his visit is a stepping stone towards further growth, deepening and strengthening of our close, broad and long-standing partnership. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar also called on President Parmelin. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar appreciated President Parmelin’s sentiments towards deepening the India-Switzerland partnership, building on the promise of India – EFTA TEPA. He expressed confidence that Mr Parmelin’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi will further engagement across a wide range of domains. The visiting dignitary paid floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat. President Parmelin will meet President Droupadi Murmu this evening. President Murmu will also host an official banquet in the honour of her Swiss Counterpart.

national_raw_news.title: President Droupadi Murmu to begin three-day visit to Himachal Pradesh today
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu will be on a three-day visit to Himachal Pradesh beginning today. The President will attend the first convocation ceremony of the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Bilaspur, as the Chief Guest today. Following the convocation ceremony, the President is scheduled to travel to Manali On the first day of her three-day visit to Himachal Pradesh, President Droupadi Murmu will attend the first convocation ceremony of AIIMS, Bilaspur, as the Chief Guest and confer degrees upon the graduating doctors. According to the proposed programme, the President will reach AIIMS at around 10:30 this morning. Governor of Himachal Pradesh Kavinder Gupta, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, and Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Jagat Prakash Nadda will also attend the convocation ceremony. On the second day of her Himachal Pradesh visit, October 7, President Murmu will visit the famous Hidimba Temple in Manali and also the Atal Tunnel in Rohtang. Meanwhile, elaborate security arrangements have been made in Bilaspur and Kullu districts in view of the President’s visit. Additional police personnel and security forces have been deployed at the AIIMS premises as well as along the routes to be taken by the President. The President is scheduled to return to Delhi on the morning of October 8.

national_raw_news.content: Best performing states, UTs under PMAY-U and PMAY 2.0 felicitated at World Habitat Day celebrations Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Best performing states, UTs under PMAY-U and PMAY 2.0 felicitated at World Habitat Day celebrations ANI | Updated: Oct 05, 2026 23:56 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 5 (ANI): The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs ( MoHUA ) celebrated World Habitat Day 2026 on the theme ‘Adequate Housing for All’ with a focus on strengthening the urban housing ecosystem through innovation, policy reforms, technology and sustainable financing. Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs Tokhan Sahu was the guest of honour of the event. Representatives of UN-Habitat, senior officials from Ministry, Principal Secretaries from States and Union Territories and other stakeholders also attended the event, marked by participation of UN agencies, HUDCO, NHB among others. The celebration provided a platform to highlight India’s continued efforts towards ensuring access to safe, affordable, inclusive and dignified housing, while recognising the contributions of States/UTs and other stakeholders towards achieving the objectives of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban (PMAY-U) and PMAY-U 2.0, a release said. The event showcased the progress and diverse approaches being adopted towards achieving the objective of “Housing for All”, including best practices under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0. As part of the PMAY-U Awards 2026, Best Performing States/UTs under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0 were felicitated, along with ULBs, partner agencies/stakeholders recognising their performance in implementing housing initiatives, including rental housing.
